I need to make sure the report says which shoppers were affected: those who had bought before but had nothing this month. I'll avoid the vague word "many" and say that instead. The peak error rate is optional, so I can include it if the placeholder is filled in. Nobody was paged. Argus reverted the feature flag, and the revert has been confirmed and is still in place. I'm weighing whether to name the affected shoppers, and I'm leaning toward saying most likely those who shopped before but bought nothing this month, keeping "likely" attached to the cause. input.overview: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed for some shoppers, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. The failure started when a new monthly spending summary was switched on for account pages. The summary runs a calculation that broke, most likely because it divides by the number of things a shopper has bought this month. That number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month, so those are most likely the shoppers who were affected. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no one on call was pulled in to respond. Argus ended the incident by switching the new summary back off, and that change is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is still a draft and has not been put into use.
